paras: The Pembroke armed posse of August 1905 was a turnout of about 25 armed citizens of Pembroke, Kentucky, on 17 August 1905, after a Black man riding a freight train shot a white brakeman near Casky. A posse led by the town marshal arrested four Black men, although the brakeman said none of them had shot him. The Hopkinsville Kentuckian said the citizens were "out for gore."

According to the Kentuckian, five Black men, among them Johnny "Bad Eye" Campbell, Ed McGaughey, Geo. McKinly and John Henry Houston, were riding a coal car of train No. 57 to the Guthrie fair. Beyond Casky, brakeman Ed Haynes tried to put them off, and one of the men shot him through both arms before the riders fled to the woods. Campbell was shot in the back from the train; the Paducah Sun said a trainman shot a rider in the neck.

Some 25 Pembroke citizens armed themselves, and Marshal Joe Jackson and a posse arrested four of the men and handed them to Sheriff Lem Davis. At Hopkinsville, Haynes viewed them on the platform and said none was the man who shot him.

City Judge Knight fined Campbell and Houston $20 each for jumping on a moving train, and the other two were to be tried the next day. A later item reported the brakeman showing signs of blood poisoning; no report of the shooter's capture was found.

Only white Kentucky papers carried the episode. The Paducah Sun's brief, "Shot By Negro Tramp," mentioned two riders but no armed citizens. The Kentuckian, under "WHITE BRAKEMAN SHOT," opened with the Pembroke turnout and warned, "woe be to the one who commits a like offense and falls into their hands." It recalled an earlier case in which, it said, "technicalities of the law" had denied the crowd "the same penalty that George Holland suffered," and said the arrested men had "an unsavory reputation."
The papers differ on the number of riders (two or five) and on the wound to the rider shot from the train, and spell the brakeman Haynes or Haney.

reader.title: Pembroke armed posse after the shooting of a brakeman (1905)
bases: After a Black man shot a white brakeman, about 25 Pembroke citizens armed themselves 'out for gore' and a marshal's posse arrested four Black men, with the paper hinting at lynching, but no violence by the citizens against the men is reported (A2).
The shooting of the brakeman is reported by three items (A1, A2, A3), but the armed gathering, the posse and the arrests appear only in the Hopkinsville Kentuckian of August 19 (A2).

accounts.label: Hopkinsville Kentuckian (local, with the brakeman's statement)
accounts.gist: Five Black men riding a coal car refused to leave; one shot the brakeman and escaped; about 25 armed Pembroke citizens turned out and the marshal's posse arrested the other four, none of whom the brakeman identified as the shooter.

accounts.label: Hopkinsville wire item
accounts.gist: Two Black men stealing a ride were being put off a freight near Casky; one shot the brakeman through both arms and the other was shot in the neck by a trainman.

framing.detail: Under 'WHITE BRAKEMAN SHOT', the Kentuckian described the citizens as 'out for gore', regretted that 'technicalities of the law' had prevented a harsher penalty in an earlier case, said the arrested men had 'an unsavory reputation' and called Campbell 'a tough character'.
The Paducah Sun ran a brief headed 'Shot By Negro Tramp' with no mention of the armed citizens.
The Kentuckian's follow-up 'BLOOD POISON' reported only the brakeman's condition.

conflicts.note: The local Kentuckian, which named four of the men, is the fuller account.
